luck.headline: Extra wins
luck.description: Actual matchup wins minus expected all-play wins. A positive number means the schedule helped.

historicalDna.scoringStrength: Within each completed season, team mean final PF per week divided by league mean final PF per week, minus one. Weighted mean of those league-relative strengths.
historicalDna.volatility: Within each completed season, population standard deviation of 14 regular-season final weekly PF divided by team mean PF. Weighted mean of season CVs.
historicalDna.classification: Use existing scoring quadrants, with weighted relative PF >= 0 for the above-league axis and weighted CV > scoring.quadrantCvBoundary for volatility.
historicalDna.availableWeights: Choose the latest up to three verified completed seasons for the same franchise and normalize available 50/30/20 weights to sum to 100%.
historicalDna.allTime: Equal-weight all verified completed seasons of the same franchise; observed quadrant persistence never recency-weighted.
historicalDna.activeSeason: Never blend ongoing 2026 data into Historical DNA; Current DNA remains separate.
historicalDna.franchiseContinuity: Explicit season + ESPN team slot mapping; 2023 ESPN slot 6 differs from 2024+.

glossary.label: Points for (PF)
glossary.summary: Total finalized fantasy points scored by a team over the selected regular-season period.
glossary.detail: A scoring measure, not a win total. Yearbook PF excludes playoff weeks.

glossary.label: PF per week
glossary.summary: Team points for divided by completed weeks in the selected period.
glossary.detail: League average PF/week is calculated over all ten teams and the same weeks.

glossary.label: Record (W–L)
glossary.summary: Wins and losses under the actual head-to-head schedule.
glossary.detail: This is not the all-play result or the PF ranking.

glossary.label: All-play record
glossary.summary: Each team's weekly final score is compared with each of the other nine teams; comparison wins and losses accumulate.
glossary.detail: Tied scores award half a comparison win each. It describes scoring strength independently of the assigned head-to-head schedule.

glossary.label: Expected wins (all-play)
glossary.summary: Each week, all-play comparison wins plus half-credit ties are divided by the nine possible opponents, then summed.
glossary.detail: This is a schedule-neutral expectation from completed scores, not a pregame forecast or playoff prediction.

glossary.label: Extra wins (schedule luck)
glossary.summary: Actual matchup wins minus expected all-play wins.
glossary.detail: Positive means the actual schedule helped relative to all-play expectation; negative means it hurt. This is the only headline luck measure.

glossary.label: Recent form
glossary.summary: Change in average PF/week between the most recent completed scoring window and the immediately preceding equal-length window.
glossary.detail: Shown as raw PF/week movement in standings and current DNA; the report card also shows movement as a percentage of season PF/week.

glossary.label: Scoring identity (DNA)
glossary.summary: A four-quadrant classification using average PF/week versus the league average and weekly scoring volatility (CV).
glossary.detail: High scoring is at or above the league baseline. High volatility is above the canonical CV boundary; categories are Volatile underdogs, High-upside wildcards, Steady lower-output, and Reliable contenders.

glossary.label: Coefficient of variation (CV)
glossary.summary: Population standard deviation of completed weekly PF divided by that team's mean weekly PF.
glossary.detail: Expressed as a percentage. Lower CV means more consistent weekly scoring relative to the average; it does not directly measure roster skill.

glossary.label: Momentum
glossary.summary: Heating up, cooling off or mostly flat based on relative change between equal-length recent and prior PF/week windows.
glossary.detail: The trend has a minimum completed-week gate and uses the shared metric thresholds, not arbitrary current-page calculations.

glossary.label: Starter-Worthy Rate (SWR)
glossary.summary: Weighted share of actual finalized starting slots meeting that week's NFL-wide positional qualification cutoffs.
glossary.detail: Seven skill slots carry weight 1 each; kicker and defense carry 0.5 each, for 8 weighted possible points. This is hindsight using final scores, not a pregame prediction.

glossary.label: Roster ceiling
glossary.summary: The maximum weighted Starter-Worthy quality attainable using the team's actual finalized starters and bench in a legal lineup.
glossary.detail: IR is excluded; the optimization permits valid slot assignments and captures what was available in hindsight, not a recommended pregame lineup.

glossary.label: Ceiling captured
glossary.summary: Actual weighted starter-worthy quality divided by the best legal weighted roster ceiling.
glossary.detail: Unavailable when no attainable qualifying ceiling exists. Higher means more of the roster's attainable hindsight quality was used.

glossary.label: Bench opportunity left
glossary.summary: Weighted lineup-quality points missed because an actual bench player could have legally improved the starting lineup.
glossary.detail: Bench upgrades are counted after optimizing assignments of existing starters, so this is separate from simply rearranging starters.

glossary.label: Unavoidable shortfall
glossary.summary: The difference between the eight possible weekly weighted quality points and the best attainable legal roster quality.
glossary.detail: Represents a roster limitation even with perfect hindsight; it is not a bench-management mistake.

glossary.label: Weekly lineup quality
glossary.summary: Starter-Worthy Rate and ceiling captured for each separately validated finalized week.
glossary.detail: Latest-week slot breakdowns and legal bench opportunities are available under Lineup.

glossary.label: Historical franchise DNA
glossary.summary: A scoring identity computed across the most recent verified completed seasons of the same permanent franchise.
glossary.detail: Weight the underlying season-relative PF and season CV first, then classify using the current canonical DNA quadrant boundaries. The ongoing 2026 season is separate.

glossary.label: PF versus league
glossary.summary: Season PF/week divided by the league's PF/week for that same season, minus one.
glossary.detail: The historical fingerprint recency-weights these league-adjusted season values; lifetime context equally weights available completed seasons.

glossary.label: Historical weekly volatility
glossary.summary: Recency-weighted average of each completed season's coefficient of variation.
glossary.detail: CV is calculated separately for each full regular season before the recency weights are applied.

glossary.label: Historical consistency
glossary.summary: How many verified completed seasons share a franchise's most frequently observed DNA quadrant.
glossary.detail: Each observed season counts equally. A tie between most common quadrants is labeled mixed rather than forced into one.

glossary.label: What-if schedule reshuffles
glossary.summary: Retrospective distributions of division finishes produced by changing weekly opponents but retaining finalized team scores.
glossary.detail: These are alternative historical schedules, not a second schedule-luck headline or an official playoff probability.

glossary.label: Scoring rank
glossary.summary: Position after sorting teams by total regular-season points for, highest first.
glossary.detail: It is not official W–L standings, division seeding, or predicted team strength.

glossary.label: Verified championship
glossary.summary: A confirmed winning franchise in the historical championship record, associated by permanent franchise ID.
glossary.detail: Trophies follow the franchise across team-name changes; unsupported earlier titles and unverified full playoff brackets are not shown.

glossary.label: Verified pregame projection comparison
glossary.summary: Actual final points compared only with explicitly verified pregame projections.
glossary.detail: Requires the canonical minimum number of independent pregame captures; in-game ESPN snapshots are excluded.
